content.comment_body: Hello, For my final year school project, I'm working on a PLC-based waste segregation system using Artificial Intelligence to identify different types of waste such as glass and plastic. I'm using a [product_name] PLC. How can I transfer data from the AI to the PLC so the PLC can respond to detected objects? I understand a PC can connect to the PLC via LAN, but how do I make the AI data compatible with the PLC for command execution? Thank you.

The [product_name] controllers only support Ethernet TCP/IP with the S7 protocol. Starting with a certain version, Modbus TCP/IP is also supported. Custom protocols cannot be implemented because the [product_name] only allows programming via ladder and function block diagrams.

Thank you. To clarify, does this mean I can use a LAN cable to load ladder logic programming to the PLC if I use the S7 protocol? I've considered using a microcontroller like Arduino to convert AI data and send it to the PLC, but that introduces more complexity such as signal amplification. Is there a simpler solution for AI-to-PLC communication? I'm struggling to find an effective way to transfer signals and data between the AI and the PLC. Your assistance is appreciated.
Is there an alternative solution? I can't provide specifics since I'm not sure how your AI interfaces. Arduino can communicate with [product_name], but I'm unfamiliar with Arduino.
Hello [user_name], [user_name]; Here’s a link to an Arduino forum entry that might be useful: [url] Hope this helps, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: A user wants to connect AI-generated outputs to a PLC for waste segregation but faces constraints from the supported protocols and programming languages. Replies clarify that only certain PLC models support necessary communication protocols and cannot implement custom ones. The user seeks straightforward AI-to-PLC data transmission but hasn't found a simple solution yet.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes for a simple and effective way to transfer AI classification results to the PLC, enabling the PLC to take action based on the detected waste material, and prefers to avoid added complexity or intermediary devices.
